item.title: Birds, gingerbread and an American: The six weirdest attacks on Sweden's Christmas goat
item.description: Every winter, people around the world turn their eyes to Gävle's Christmas goat, eagerly waiting to see if it survives the Christmas season. Here's a look at some of the most outrageous attempts to destroy the iconic straw goat throughout its history.

item.title: OPINION: Three reasons to make English an official language in Sweden
item.description: Magnus Hambleton, a partner at the Swedish tech fund byFounders, argues that if Sweden were to make English an official national language, it would open itself up to an entire world of talent.

item.title: HOOONNNK! What's that noise? No need to freak out, Sweden
item.description: Don't be alarmed if you hear a long, deafening siren on Monday afternoon in Sweden. It is just 'Hoarse Fredrik' – and it is only a test.

item.description: Here's one of Sweden's most famous Christmas characters.

item.title: How new Swedish migration rules could affect foreign residents in 2026
item.description: Several major changes to Swedish migration laws are expected in 2026. Here are the ones likely to have the biggest impact on the lives of foreigners in Sweden.

item.title: Why northern Swedes feel ignored and underappreciated
item.description: Just because northern Swedes can be good-humoured about southern prejudice doesn’t mean it doesn’t bother them. Behind the jokes there are some very material resentments, and a complicated history.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Nordic countries becoming more sedentary, property prices fell last month and neo-Nazi group granted permit for new march. Here's Sweden's news on Tuesday.

item.title: 'Let him starve': Internal reports reveal issues at Swedish migrant detention centres
item.description: A set of internal incident reports from detention centres operated by the Swedish Migration Agency, obtained by The Local, has revealed accusations of racist and degrading behaviour from detention centre staff, and poor conditions pushing detainees to violence or self-harm.

item.title: Swedish property prices fall in November
item.description: Property prices fell last month, although when seasonal effects are taken into account they actually rose slightly, according to a monthly property price indicator from SBAB Booli. But it's not all good news ‒ the number of properties sold was low.

item.title: 'Grim reading': New report shows Nordic countries eating worse and moving less
item.description: Residents of the Nordic countries ‒ Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Iceland and Finland ‒ are eating more meat and less fruit and veg, moving less and getting heavier, a new report on lifestyles in the region has shown.
